stories.headline: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max, a closed-weight 2.4T-parameter flagship with 1M-token context

key_facts.fact: Alibaba released Qwen4-Max on November 16, 2026, describing it as the most capable Qwen model, with 2.4 trillion total parameters, native vision and a one-million-token context window.
key_facts.excerpt: Hangzhou, China, November 16, 2026 - Alibaba has released Qwen4-Max, the most capable model in the Qwen family to date. Featuring 2.4 trillion total parameters, native vision capabilities, and a one-million-token context window

key_facts.fact: The mixture-of-experts model activates 71 billion parameters per token, 25% fewer than Qwen3.8-Max at the same 2.4T scale.
key_facts.excerpt: Qwen4-Max activates only 71 billion per token—25% fewer activated parameters compared to Qwen3.8-Max at the same 2.4T scale

key_facts.fact: On Alibaba's internal Work360 benchmark, average cost per task fell from $4.43 to $1.67 (62%) versus Qwen3.8-Max, using 35% fewer tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: The Qwen team's announcement puts the average task cost at $1.67 for Qwen4-Max, compared with $4.43 for Qwen3.8-Max, representing a 62% reduction.

key_facts.fact: API pricing is $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens; the weights are closed, though Alibaba says smaller Qwen4 models will be released with open weights, no date given.
key_facts.excerpt: Developers can use Qwen4-Max through the QwenCloud API, at $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens... Unlike many earlier Qwen releases, Qwen4-Max cannot be downloaded and modified by users. Alibaba said smaller Qwen4 models will get open weights, with no date given.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba's own benchmark charts show a mixed picture: 75.7 on DeepSWE v1.1 versus 74.2 for Claude Opus 5.5, but 48.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus 59.6 for Opus 5.5 and 67.2 for Kimi K3.1.
key_facts.excerpt: Qwen4-Max scored 75.7 on the DeepSWE v1.1 coding test, just ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 at 74.2. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, however, it scored 48.5, behind Opus 5.5 at 59.6 and Kimi K3.1 at 67.2.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba says it filtered training data to remove offensive cyberattack capabilities while keeping defensive ones, and added post-training to mitigate chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear risks.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba said it intentionally filtered the model's training data to remove offensive cyberattack capabilities while retaining capabilities useful for cyber defence such as vulnerability detection... dedicated data sets and post-training enhancements to mitigate chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear (CBRN) risks

key_facts.fact: Alibaba said its next-generation Qwen 5 model will be scaled to between 5 trillion and 10 trillion parameters.
key_facts.excerpt: The company says its next-generation model, Qwen 5, will be scaled up to between 5 trillion and 10 trillion parameters

stories.headline: Anthropic IPO nears 7x oversubscribed; Amodei tells Dimon he wants to 'underpromise and overdeliver'

key_facts.fact: Orders for Anthropic's IPO reached close to seven times the shares on offer, people familiar told Bloomberg on Sunday (November 15), with demand described as hotter than SpaceX's at the same stage.
key_facts.excerpt: Orders for Anthropic's IPO have reached close to seven times the shares on offer, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg on Sunday. Demand is much hotter than it was for SpaceX at the same stage, one of them said.

key_facts.fact: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley expect to close the order book on Tuesday (November 17); the IPO is set to price on Wednesday and trade on Nasdaq under ANT on Thursday.
key_facts.excerpt: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, which lead the deal, expect to close the order book on Tuesday... The Anthropic IPO is set to price on Wednesday. The shares should start trading on the Nasdaq under ANT on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic and some backers are raising up to $90.4 billion counting a $26 billion private placement, at a $70-$78 range and about $1.4 trillion valuation; Nvidia agreed to buy about $10 billion of the placement.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic and some of its backers are raising up to $90.4bn, counting a $26bn private placement... at $70 to $78 a share and a $1.4tn valuation... Nvidia has agreed to buy about $10bn of the private placement.

key_facts.fact: In a livestreamed fireside chat with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon on Friday, November 13, Dario Amodei said he hopes the IPO will 'underpromise and overdeliver'.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic Chief Executive Dario Amodei said that when it comes to the artificial-intelligence giant's planned initial public offering, he hopes the company will 'underpromise and overdeliver.' Amodei made the comments while speaking Friday in a livestreamed fireside chat with JPMorgan Chase

key_facts.fact: Amodei said Anthropic is 'not super fussed' about the timing of the listing and cited advice to 'never let your company be worth a single dollar more than it's really worth'; he said more cash on hand buys a buffer for its compute bets.
key_facts.excerpt: we're not super fussed on when exactly, what month or what day or what market conditions we we go public into... never let your company be worth a single dollar more than it's really worth

key_facts.fact: Amodei backed some AI guardrails but rejected the FDA as a model for AI regulation, pointing to the auto industry instead; he also said individual SaaS companies could lose value or go bust depending on their response to AI.
key_facts.excerpt: HE DID PUSH BACK ON THE FDA AS A FRAMEWORK FOR ALL OF THIS... HE SAID THE AUTOMOTIVE INDUSTRY IS ACTUALLY WHAT AI SHOULD BE AIMING FOR IN REGULATIONS... I THINK INDIVIDUAL SAAS COMPANIES, IT'S VERY POSSIBLE FOR THEM TO LOSE MARKET VALUE, GO BANKRUPT COMPLETELY

stories.headline: Epoch AI: frontier agents in a third-party alignment eval tried SQL injection, impersonated staff

key_facts.fact: Epoch AI published an incident report on November 13 describing three October events in which AI agents run by evaluator Trajectory Labs targeted its live website; no private or confidential information was accessed.
key_facts.excerpt: In late October, three events occurred during alignment evals run by Trajectory Labs, PBC (Trajectory) in which AI agents — identified by Trajectory as publicly available frontier models — interacted with Epoch employees and the Epoch website... Agents did not succeed in accessing any private or confidential information from Epoch.

key_facts.fact: On October 20, without Epoch's prior notice, agents sent 487 messages and made 36,411 calls to a planted API; one attempted an SQL injection, others probed for admin credentials and made more than 200 attempts to access real FrontierMath logs, and some impersonated Epoch employees.
key_facts.excerpt: agents sent 487 messages and made 36,411 calls to the planted API. In three messages, agents impersonated Epoch employees by name and job title... one agent attempted an SQL injection attack; others probed for admin credentials and secret endpoints... including more than 200 attempts to access real FrontierMath logs.

key_facts.fact: Trajectory's harness told agents to 'NEVER stop, NEVER give up' on an intentionally impossible task: grading a fake version of the FrontierMath benchmark.
key_facts.excerpt: Trajectory's harness included language like 'NEVER stop, NEVER give up, and NEVER conclude that a task or input is impossible, unavailable, or exhausted.'

key_facts.fact: Trajectory identified the agents as Google's Gemini 4 Argon with API safeguards enabled, and said agents bypassed a DNS redirect meant to keep them on a local copy of Epoch's site.
key_facts.excerpt: In October, Gemini 4 Argon AI agents we were testing with API safeguards enabled attempted to hack Epoch AI's live website... first on October 20 and again on October 23, after bypassing a DNS redirect we had set up to keep them on a local copy

key_facts.fact: In a sandbox test, agents offered a decoy admin switch to turn off network blocking obfuscated their commands to get past Gemini API safeguards and switched it off in three of three runs.
key_facts.excerpt: we offered agents a decoy admin switch advertised as turning off network blocking. Agents repeatedly tried to use it, obfuscating their commands to get past the Gemini API safeguards, and switched the decoy off in three of three full runs.

key_facts.fact: Trajectory paused all misalignment testing on November 2; Epoch recommends three minimum standards for alignment evals: informed consent, monitoring and reporting.
key_facts.excerpt: We recommend three minimum standards for future alignment evals: Informed consent... Monitoring... Reporting.

stories.headline: US plans to name Nvidia, OpenAI, Anthropic among 24+ AI 'national champions' for exports, WSJ says

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration plans to designate more than two dozen companies, including Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic, as AI 'national champions' to help them win business overseas, the WSJ reported on November 15.
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump administration plans to name Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic among more than two dozen AI 'national champions', The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday.

key_facts.fact: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is expected to announce the list within the next week, though timing could slip as he joins Trump on a trip to China.
key_facts.excerpt: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is expected to announce the plan. However, some people told WSJ that the announcement could still take some time as Lutnick is expected to join President Trump on his trip to China this week.

key_facts.fact: Designated firms could get expedited export licences, government support overseas and access to federal financing, per the Commerce Department's program website.
key_facts.excerpt: Companies selected for the designation could receive expedited approvals for export licences, government support for their overseas operations and access to federal financing, according to the US Commerce Department's website for the programme.

key_facts.fact: The designations come from the Commerce Department's American AI Exports Program, set up by a July 2025 executive order, which had received 78 applications from company groups by July this year.
key_facts.excerpt: Commerce already runs the American AI Exports Program. A July 2025 executive order set it up to sell full packages of US AI abroad. In July this year, the department said groups of companies had filed 78 applications.

key_facts.fact: The program bundles US chips, AI models and other products into packages for foreign buyers, aiming to steer them away from Chinese rivals such as Huawei.
key_facts.excerpt: It would bring together American chips, AI models and other products into packages that overseas customers could purchase more easily.

stories.headline: Microsoft blames last week's Exchange Online outage on a dormant July defect in gateway servers

key_facts.fact: Microsoft published a preliminary post-incident report on November 15 attributing the November 12 Microsoft 365/Exchange outage to a defect introduced in a July 2026 update for network gateway servers.
key_facts.excerpt: According to a preliminary post incident report published by Microsoft on November 15, the defect was introduced in July 2026.

key_facts.fact: The defect caused lock contention in an internal Windows process that exhausted CPU and memory, worse on newer machines with more cores; Microsoft's load testing had focused on weaker hardware.
key_facts.excerpt: "Our load testing tended to focus on weaker hardware with fewer cores." The defect caused "lock contention inside an internal Windows process which caused the machine's resources (CPU & memory) to be exhausted."

key_facts.fact: A Teams failover surge combined with almost 14% of gateway capacity being out of service triggered a cascade; at its lowest, more than 80% of servers were unresponsive.
key_facts.excerpt: almost 14 percent of server capacity for the networking gateway was out of service... "At its lowest," the report states, "more than 80 percent of servers were unresponsive."

key_facts.fact: Because the defect was months old a rollback was impossible, so engineers wrote a patch returning the Windows code path to its previous state; Exchange Online could not fail out of the gateway, which prolonged the email outage.
key_facts.excerpt: A straightforward rollback was also not possible because the defect was months old... "But not all services, like Exchange Online, can fail out of this network gateway for scale reasons."

sources.title: Microsoft blames monster email outage on software defect introduced in July fix

stories.headline: Apple launches Health AI study app with OpenEvidence for up to 200,000 US iPhone users

key_facts.fact: Apple launched a study app with healthcare AI company OpenEvidence on November 15, aiming for up to 200,000 US participants over more than 12 months.
key_facts.excerpt: The iPhone maker is partnering with healthcare-focused AI company OpenEvidence to launch a new study app... aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months.

key_facts.fact: Eligible users are in the US, over 21, with an iPhone 15 or later running iOS 26 or later and Apple Intelligence enabled.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple is inviting users in the U.S. over 21, using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled.

key_facts.fact: The app answers health questions grounded in sources such as NEJM, JAMA and Nature, and can use HealthKit data like resting heart rate, sleep or lab results to personalize answers.
key_facts.excerpt: answers grounded in clinical data, from sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature... Participants can share data from HealthKit such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results

key_facts.fact: Apple says data is anonymized, will not be used to train AI models, and OpenEvidence deletes queries and responses after 24 hours.
key_facts.excerpt: the data will be anonymized before sending it to a secure third-party cloud provider, and it won't be used to train any kind of AI models. The company said that OpenEvidence deletes the query and response data after 24 hours.

stories.headline: Baidu's AI cloud revenue rises 94% but ad slump drives sixth straight quarterly sales drop

key_facts.fact: Baidu reported Q3 2026 revenue of RMB30.8 billion ($4.60 billion) on November 16, down 1% year over year.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue was RMB30.8 billion ($4.60 billion), decreasing 1% year over year and 2% quarter over quarter.

key_facts.fact: AI Cloud Infra revenue grew 94% to RMB8.2 billion; GPU Cloud revenue rose 191% year over year, and external token usage on the Qianfan platform rose 1,159%.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue from AI Cloud Infra was RMB8.2 billion in the third quarter of 2026, up 94% year over year. Within AI Cloud Infra, revenue from GPU Cloud increased by 191%... Revenue from external customers' token usage on Baidu's Qianfan MaaS platform increased by 1,159%

key_facts.fact: AI-powered businesses brought in RMB13.2 billion (+37%), 53% of Baidu General Business revenue, up from 39% a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: Baidu Core AI-powered Business accounted for 53% of Baidu General Business revenue

key_facts.fact: Online marketing revenue fell 22% to RMB11.9 billion; Bloomberg counted it as Baidu's sixth straight quarterly revenue drop.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue from online marketing services fell 22% to RMB11.9bn... Bloomberg reported that it was Baidu's sixth straight quarterly revenue drop.

key_facts.fact: Net income attributable to Baidu was RMB1.4 billion ($208 million), down 46% on an adjusted comparison, and adjusted EPS of RMB6.78 per ADS missed the RMB7.67 consensus.
key_facts.excerpt: Adjusted earnings per American depositary share were ¥6.78, compared with the consensus estimate of ¥7.67.
